messages:
priya: Heads-up — the overnight compression run for qx2b (float16->int8) dropped perf on our verification cohort by ~3.2%. Not just throughput: we're seeing early truncation on long-instruction/list prompts and some entity drop.
matt: ugh. Is this isolated to the int8 build or saw in int4 too? any config diff? :thinking_face:
priya: mainly int8. int4 was worse but we hadn't pushed that wide. Kernel selection changed (fast-kv packing) + a new activation clipping patch.
sara: can you paste a minimal repro prompt/example? also which slices in the verification cohort regressed most?
priya: example prompt that failed: "Compare these two shopping lists and preserve bullets; do not invent items." model output cut off mid-list.
priya: top regressed slices: long_instructions, dense-bullet-lists, and multi-entity-table-merge.
anya: we should assemble a small "sanity corpus" of edge cases and run differential diffs across runtimes. I can pull 200 candidate items from production logs (sanitized) if we add decontamination checks.
priya: yes please. before ingest we need decontam: no PII, no customer text. add provenance tags.
priya: local eval command I ran:
```
./eval/run.sh --model qx2b-int8 --cohort=verification --slices=long_instructions,lists --out=artifacts/qx2b-int8-2026-03-20.json
```
ops-qa: tagging: label team can do a 200-item micro-run, ETA ~48h for relabel + triage.
matt: while that's happening we should put a slice-aware fallback in the routing rules: for queries matching long_instructions or lists -> route to qx2b-f16 until we confirm.
priya: Agreed. I'll open a console route patch and attach the condition. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/routes/qx2b-canary (privileged link)
deploy-bot: Canary quality alert triggered: qx2b-int8 — quality_drop > 2% on verification cohort. Autoswitch to fallback route applied.
anya: I'll curate the 200 candidates into `sanity_corpus_v1` and tag with expected-fail-mode: truncation/stylistic-loss/missing-entities. Need volunteers to review 50 items each.
sara: I can take 75 (long instructions + lists).
matt: I'll take the multi-entity table cases (50).
ops-qa: label pipeline: will create a relabel job, mapping: expected vs. actual, severity. ETA 48h after job creation.
priya: thanks all. After relabel results we can run pairwise evals (f16 vs int8) and produce a short remediation plan (disable clipping patch or tweak kernel packing).
anya: also recommend adding a small unit-test to the eval harness for list-preservation (pre/post diff) so regressions get caught earlier.
priya: good call. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow 10:00am PT to review the sanity corpus and decide rollback vs patch. cc @sara @matt @anya :thumbsup:
sara: noted, see you tomorrow.
matt: thanks, will stand by for the console patch review.
